name: Iselsberg-Stronach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village at the Iselsbergpass, offering stunning views of the Lienzer Dolomiten and the Großglockner.
beschreibung:
Overview

Iselsberg-Stronach is perched at an altitude of 1,117 metres in the district of Lienz, East Tyrol, gracefully terraced along the sun-drenched southern slopes of the Schober Group at the historic Iselsberg Pass (1,209 m). This scenic pass connects the Lienz valley basin with the Möll Valley in Carinthia and the High Tauern National Park. Home to approximately 610 residents, the municipality comprises the twin hamlets of Iselsberg and Stronach, spanning elevations from 750 metres to over 2,200 metres. Celebrated as one of Tyrol's most breathtaking natural viewing balconies, the village affords uninterrupted panoramic vistas of the craggy limestone peaks of the Lienz Dolomites, including the Spitzkofel and Laserzwand. Free from hectic mass tourism, it provides pure alpine air, living agricultural customs, and serene hiking trails.

History

The Iselsberg Pass has served as a key transalpine route since antiquity: A fortified Roman mountain road linked the Roman municipality of Aguntum in the valley with alpine gold mines and ancient settlements in Carinthia. In medieval times, a customs outpost guarded the frontier between the County of Gorizia and Carinthia. The earliest written documentation appears in the 13th century as Iselsperge, named after the Isel river. Stronach earned international acclaim as the birthplace of celebrated painter Franz von Defregger (1835–1921), born at the historic Ederhof farmstead, whose iconic historical and rustic canvases defined Tyrolean art. Today, the Ederhof functions as a specialized pediatric rehabilitation centre housing a Defregger memorial site. The Baroque Guardian Angel Church (Schutzengelkirche) in Iselsberg was built between 1757 and 1759 to protect travellers negotiating the steep mountain pass.

Getting There

Iselsberg-Stronach is easily accessed by road and public transit. Motorists from Lienz take the federal highway B100 to Dölsach, turning onto the scenic B107 Großglockner federal road, which climbs via sweeping curves to Iselsberg in about ten minutes (10 km). Coming from Salzburg or Carinthia, the B107 leads from Winklern across the Iselsberg Pass straight into Tyrol. Rail passengers travel on ÖBB services to Lienz railway station. Outside the station, regional bus route 942 operates regular daily services toward Winklern and Heiligenblut, stopping at several convenient stations across the municipality.

Tips

A must-visit is the "Schöne Aussicht" panoramic terrace, offering commanding views across the entire Lienz basin and the soaring Dolomites. Art lovers should stroll along the Defregger Trail from Dölsach up to Stronach to explore the painter's early life and legacy. Hikers will delight in the trek up to the Roaner Alm at 1,903 metres, celebrated for authentic East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen pasta pockets and spectacular panoramas, followed by an ascent to Mount Ederplan (1,962 m) and its landmark summit cross. In winter, panoramic cross-country ski trails and peaceful winter walking routes await, while Lienz's ski resorts (Zettersfeld and Hochstein) lie just 15 minutes away.
